2608.28790.title: ASTRA - Agentic System for Ticket Resolution and Analysis
2608.28790.paper_summary: Technical operations teams resolve large volumes of incidents by synthesizing fragmented evidence from ticket text, historical cases, system logs, and technical documentation. Existing automation often relies on monolithic generation without explicit evidence modeling or provenance, making outputs difficult to verify when critical signals are sparse across sources. We propose ASTRA, an agentic system for ticket resolution in which a central orchestrator coordinates three specialist information-gathering agents and drives a judge-orchestrator refinement loop to produce evidence-backed troubleshooting reports. TicketSimilarityAgent retrieves relevant historical precedents through dense retrieval and LLM reranking; LogAgent distills hundreds of thousands of log lines into structured, quote-grounded findings using deterministic filtering and constrained LLM analysis; and DomainKnowledgeAgent retrieves relevant technical knowledge via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Their outputs are transformed into a claim-evidence representation linking each claim to a verbatim source passage, assigning a support level, and preventing cross-attribution. A JudgeAgent scores the report on five criteria, while the OrchestratorAgent converts low scores into targeted follow-up queries for bounded iterative refinement. Evaluated on 987 real-world telecom fault tickets across seven product lines, ASTRA achieves a mean quality score of 4.13/5.0, with 59.9% of reports identifying the fault area at the component-family level or better. Relevance and Clarity scores are 4.88 and 4.94, respectively, while fabricated technical details remain below 3% of error cases. Stratification by fault type reveals that hardware faults remain substantially harder than software or configuration faults (Cohen's d=0.80), pointing to a fundamental limitation of text-based evidence channels for hardware fault diagnosis.
2608.28790.paper_summary_zh: 技術操作團隊透過合成來自票據文本、歷史案例、系統日誌和技術文檔的零散證據，解決大量事件。現有的自動化通常依賴於單一生成，缺乏明確的證據建模或來源，當關鍵信號在各來源中稀疏時，產出難以驗證。我們提出了ASTRA，一個用於票據解決的代理系統，其中一個中央協調者協調三個專業信息收集代理，並推動一個評審-協調者精煉循環，以生成基於證據的故障排除報告。TicketSimilarityAgent通過密集檢索和LLM重新排名檢索相關的歷史先例；LogAgent使用確定性過濾和受限的LLM分析，將數十萬條日誌行提煉成結構化的、基於引用的發現；DomainKnowledgeAgent通過模型上下文協議（MCP）檢索相關的技術知識。它們的輸出被轉換為一個主張-證據表示，將每個主張鏈接到逐字的來源段落，分配支持級別，並防止交叉歸因。一個JudgeAgent根據五個標準對報告進行評分，而OrchestratorAgent將低分轉換為針對性的後續查詢，以便進行有限的迭代精煉。在對七個產品線的987個實際電信故障票據進行評估時，ASTRA達到了4.13/5.0的平均質量分數，59.9%的報告在組件-家族級別或更高的水平上識別故障區域。相關性和清晰度分數分別為4.88和4.94，而虛構的技術細節仍低於3%的錯誤案例。按故障類型分層顯示，硬體故障仍然比軟體或配置故障難得多（Cohen's d=0.80），這指出了基於文本的證據渠道在硬體故障診斷中的基本限制。
